transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE); Raj Patel (Redwood SE); Tom Alvarez (Vega CTO); Priya Shah (Head of ML); Ethan Moore (Infra)
Shared links: benchmark spreadsheet - https://bit.ly/vega-bench, SOC2 pack - internal link (sent after)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery focused on latency and throughput targets for inference. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) options. Discussed p95 SLAs, concurrency, streaming, and token/sec benchmarking. Agreed next steps to run POC benchmarks and share security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Lena from Redwood. Raj from our SE team is with me. Tom, Priya, Ethan — thanks for making time. How's everyone?
[00:12] Tom (CTO): Good, thanks. Busy week but excited. We wanted to dig into latency requirements and what the different deployment options look like for us.
[00:20] Priya (Head of ML): Yeah, mostly around p95 targets and concurrency. For our user-facing product we need p95 generation under 300ms for short prompts (~64 tokens) and around 800ms for 512 tokens — roughly. Also we do streaming for part of the UI so tail behavior is important.
[00:38] Raj (SE): Got it. Realistic targets. Are those end-to-end (including network) or server-side only?
[00:43] Priya: End-to-end, from client to token visible in the UI. We run in GCP europe-west1.
[00:49] Lena: Okay that's helpful. Quick question on throughput - what's your concurrency and token/sec expectations?
[00:55] Ethan (Infra): Right now typical concurrency is around 80 active users, but peak concurrency during marketing pushes can get to 400. For token/sec we see bursts up to 12k tokens/sec across the fleet, sustained around 3-4k.
[01:10] Raj: Thanks. That helps sizing. A couple things to call out: hosted API is fastest to try, but Dedicated gives predictable throughput and reserved GPU pools which matter at your scale. Private (VPC/on-prem) is an option if you need network isolation or specific KMS/HSM integrations.
[01:26] Tom: We're evaluating cost vs latency. If we do hosted, do you have p95 numbers with streaming enabled? We've seen weird jitter with other vendors.
[01:35] Raj: Yes — we have internal profiles. For a 13B open model on NVIDIA A10-ish class we typically see server-side p95 generation for 64 tokens around 100-140ms when batching is limited and KV cache hits are used. With streaming there can be small added serialization overhead but we prioritize first-token latency; the p95 for first token is often similar. But real numbers depend on prompt shape, model, and whether you enable quantization.
[01:58] Priya: Interesting — our biggest worry is tail during concurrency spikes. We can't afford 2s p95. How does Redwood handle overload?
[02:06] Raj: We do smart routing and fallbacks. For Dedicated you can set autoscaling and burst policies; for hosted we route by region and can fall back to compatible lower-cost model variants if the primary is saturated. We also do KV/prefix caching so repeat prompts come back much faster. There are tradeoffs around cost though.
[02:26] Ethan: For private deployment we need SSO and SAML integration, KMS key control and audit logs. Also SOC2 is a must for procurement.
[02:34] Lena: Yep we can share SOC2, ISO artefacts and a network diagram. For KMS we integrate with customer-managed keys in VPC/private modes; hosted supports envelope encryption with our KMS but we can do dedicated HSM options for private deployments.
[02:50] Tom: On benchmarking — we'd like Redwood to run a token/sec benchmark using our prompts. Do you have a standard harness?
[02:57] Raj: Yes we have a benchmark harness. Ideally we get a sample prompt set and traffic profile. We run both server-side token/sec and end-to-end client latency tests. We'll provide raw logs and a spreadsheet with p50/p90/p95 and token/sec. We can run on hosted first, then repeat on Dedicated sizing and Private if you want.
[03:16] Priya: Would quantized model variants affect p95 significantly? We tried 4-bit quant on other infra and saw slight tail variance.
[03:23] Raj: Good question. Quantization often reduces throughput cost and can improve latency for some models, but it depends on kernel selection. Our runtime picks optimized kernels and some quantized paths are actually faster at inference on certain hardware; others can add variance. We'll include quantized and float baselines in the benchmark.
[03:40] Ethan: For concurrency management do you support per-customer rate limiting and token-level billing breakdowns for cost analysis?
[03:46] Lena: Yes, console shows per-route and per-token cost and latency breakdowns. You can set quotas and rate limits per API key.
[03:53] Tom: What's the billing model for Dedicated? Flat monthly reserved plus usage bursts?
[03:58] Lena: Typically reserved capacity with monthly commit, plus burst capacity at a delta rate. We can provide a sizing recommendation and pricing tiers — that's part of the action item.
[04:08] Priya: For the POC we want a 2-week Dedicated trial if possible to see sustained throughput. Is that something you do?
[04:15] Raj: We can often spin up a trial Dedicated queue for qualified customers. We'll coordinate with sales. For the technical POC we'll need your dataset and representative traffic.
[04:24] Ethan: Network wise our infra sits in a private subnet and we need to avoid egress to public internet for sensitive prompts. How would Redwood integrate?
[04:31] Raj: For Private we can deploy inside your VPC or give a customer-managed gateway. For hosted we support VPC peering or private link options depending on cloud. We'll include network diagrams in the docs we send.
[04:45] Tom: Competitors question — we've been testing OpenAI embeddings and Anthropic for chat; how do you think Redwood compares on tail latency and cost?
[04:54] Lena: Redwood is a platform — we run and optimize models. On tail latency we focus on runtime optimizations (KV cache, continuous batching) and routing policies. Cost-wise our optimize toolkit gives suggestions for batching/quantization. We'll share benchmark examples versus third-party public numbers but the most useful is the POC with your prompts.
[05:12] Priya: Sounds good. A couple of nitty-gritty: p95 SLAs — do you provide contractual p95 guarantees for Hosted? For Dedicated?
[05:20] Raj: Hosted has best-effort SLOs; Dedicated can have SLA-backed latency and uptime targets depending on the contract level. For Private we can include SLA terms as part of enterprise licensing. We'll include sample SLA language in the docs.
[05:33] Ethan: Any suggestions to get deterministic lower p95? We've tried pre-warming and static batching but still see variance.
[05:39] Raj: Pre-warm is useful; so is a small percentile of reserved capacity to absorb bursts. Also short sequence length models and prefix caching help. We can also recommend routing to smaller sequence-optimized model variants for interactive paths.
[05:56] Lena: Ok to recap next steps: I'll send pricing and Dedicated sizing, Raj will prep benchmark plan and sample prompts, Ethan will share dataset and traffic profile, and we'll schedule a 2-hour POC next week.
[06:08] Tom: Yep that works. Also please include SOC2 and the network diagram.
[06:12] Lena: Will do. Anything else?
[06:16] Priya: One more — can you run a quick streaming first-token p95 test as a teaser on hosted? Even a single sample run would be helpful.
[06:24] Raj: Absolutely, we can do a quick run and send the raw logs.
[06:28] Tom: Great, thanks everyone.
[06:30] Lena: Thanks, we'll follow up with the items.

End of call.
